solidworks_gui_assert_no_modal.doc: Check that no modal dialog is open and raise if one is, so it cannot swallow the next input. Read-only, and it neither clicks nor closes anything; call it before every action.

params.main_hwnd: Main window handle to inspect; 0 lets the tool find the SolidWorks window itself. Defaults to 0.
params.where: Text written into the error message to say which action found the dialog. Defaults to empty.

solidworks_gui_close_modals.doc: Close every modal dialog and report how many were closed after verifying that each window really disappeared. Modifies the desktop, not the model: a hanging window never consumes its messages, so a message is posted first and real input events are the fallback.

params.main_hwnd: Main window handle to inspect; 0 lets the tool find the SolidWorks window itself. Defaults to 0.
params.rounds: Maximum number of scan, click and verify rounds. Defaults to 1.

solidworks_gui_focus_state.doc: Report whether the wanted window is really in the foreground. Read-only state check through the Win32 foreground window, so use it before an action instead of assuming the window took focus.

params.want: Window handle that is expected to be in the foreground.

solidworks_gui_ensure_focus.doc: Set a window as the foreground window, then read the foreground window back to confirm it really happened. Modifies desktop focus only, not the model, and reports failure instead of assuming success.

params.hwnd: Window handle to put in the foreground.
params.retries: Number of focus attempts. Defaults to 5.
params.settle_seconds: Seconds to wait between attempts. Defaults to 0.2.

solidworks_gui_assert_focus.doc: Check that the wanted window has focus, repair it when it does not, and raise when the repair fails. Call it before every action; a silent continue would drop every later keystroke with no visible sign.

params.hwnd: Window handle that should be in the foreground.
params.where: Text written into the error message to say which action found the wrong focus. Defaults to empty.

solidworks_surface_runtime_available.doc: Report whether one IModeler surface method is proven usable on this machine, where unmeasured methods return false. Read-only lookup in this repo's measured runtime table, not a live SolidWorks call.

params.method: Member name to look up, for example CreateCylindricalSurface or its numbered variant.

solidworks_motion_create_study.doc: Create a Motion Study on the active assembly and return it. Writes a study into the assembly and does not save the document; the active document must be an assembly, and a non-assembly is reported rather than guessed.

params.name: Study name; omitting it keeps the SolidWorks default name. Defaults to no name.
params.duration: Study duration in seconds, not a length. Defaults to 4.0.
params.study_type: Motion Study type enum value; when omitted the SolidWorks default type is kept. Defaults to no value.

solidworks_motion_collect_summary.doc: Return a JSON-able summary of every motion study in the assembly: type, duration, motor count and result status. Read-only; it never modifies a study, and results_out_of_date true means the study must be calculated again.

solidworks_motion_validate_studies.doc: Validate the motion studies against the given requirements and return the result. Read-only: it reports, it does not fix, and the returned asked key lists which requirements were actually applied.

params.study_name: Only validate this study; omitting it validates every available study. Defaults to no filter.
params.expected_study_type: Required study type enum value; omitting it accepts any type. Defaults to no requirement.
params.minimum_duration_seconds: Minimum study duration in seconds. Defaults to no requirement.
params.minimum_motor_count: Minimum number of motors. Defaults to no requirement.
params.require_results: Whether the study must have computed, non-stale results. Defaults to no requirement.

solidworks_motion_study_manager.doc: Return the Motion Study manager object of the active assembly, the entry point for the other motion tools. Read-only; loading the Motion type library first avoids members that behave like properties instead of methods.

params.load_type_library: Whether to load the Motion type library first, which a fresh session needs. Defaults to true.

solidworks_motion_ensure_type_library.doc: Check whether the Motion Study type library is loaded, load it if needed, and return its path. Use it before asking anything else from Motion: without swmotionstudy.tlb the manager members misbehave as properties instead of methods.

params.raise_on_error: Whether to raise instead of returning false when the library cannot be found or loaded. Defaults to false.

solidworks_motion_validate_summary.doc: Validate a motion-study summary dict against delivery requirements and return status, checks and issues. Read-only, pure data with no SolidWorks call; it re-checks a summary recorded earlier.

params.summary: Summary dict as returned by solidworks_motion_collect_summary.
params.study_name: Only validate this study; omitting it validates every available study. Defaults to no filter.
params.expected_study_type: Required study type enum value; omitting it accepts any type. Defaults to no requirement.
params.minimum_duration_seconds: Minimum study duration in seconds. Defaults to no requirement.
params.minimum_motor_count: Minimum number of motors. Defaults to no requirement.
params.require_results: Whether the study must have computed, non-stale results. Defaults to no requirement.

solidworks_chamfer.doc: Chamfer the selected edges of the active part with a distance and angle pair. Writes a chamfer feature and does not save the document; the edge comes from the selection argument because the API acts on the current selection only.

params.selection: Declarative edge selection: '__current_selection__' to keep what is already selected, or 'index:<n>' for the n-th edge on the body, counted from 0.
params.angle_deg: Chamfer angle in degrees. Defaults to 45.

solidworks_fillet.doc: Round the selected edges of the active part with a fillet radius. Writes a fillet feature and does not save the document; the edge comes from the selection argument because the API acts on the current selection only.

params.selection: Declarative edge selection: '__current_selection__' to keep what is already selected, or 'index:<n>' for the n-th edge on the body, counted from 0.

solidworks_feature_suppress.doc: Suppress one named feature of the active document. Writes the suppression into the model and does not save; the feature is selected by name first and an empty selection raises instead of silently doing nothing.

params.feature_name: Feature name exactly as it appears in the FeatureManager tree, for example the boss-extrude entry.

solidworks_feature_unsuppress.doc: Unsuppress one named feature of the active document. Writes the model back to its unsuppressed state and does not save; it uses the same selection contract and refusal guard as solidworks_feature_suppress.

params.feature_name: Feature name exactly as it appears in the FeatureManager tree.

solidworks_feature_delete.doc: Delete one named feature of the active document. Writes the deletion into the model and does not save; the call returns nothing, so success shows as the feature disappearing from the tree, and an empty selection is refused.

params.feature_name: Feature name exactly as it appears in the FeatureManager tree, for example the boss-extrude entry.

solidworks_costing_include_body.doc: Set whether one body counts in the cost calculation, addressed by name. Writes the inclusion flag on the costing body and does not save; it is not yet verified on a real machine, so list the body names first with solidworks_costing_list_bodies.

params.body_name: Name of the body as listed by solidworks_costing_list_bodies; it is a name, not a coordinate.
params.include: Whether the body counts in the cost calculation, where true includes it and false excludes it. Defaults to true.

solidworks_costing_set_method.doc: Set the value of one costing method by name. Writes to the costing model and is not yet verified on a real machine; the integer value has no published meaning, so it is passed through unchanged.

params.method: Integer method value; the allowed values are undocumented, so the tool passes it through without interpreting it.

solidworks_costing_update_cost_for_all_b.doc: Update the cost of every body in the active part after a material, template or inclusion change. Writes the refreshed cost figures and is not yet verified on a real machine; it takes no arguments, so call it once those earlier settings are in place.
